critique.good: Destination names are easy to scan, delivery ranges stay together, and the header hierarchy is clear.
critique.problems: The conditions form an extremely narrow, choppy text column. Tall rows leave large empty areas under the destinations and windows, making comparisons across rows laborious.
critique.cause: The 159px destination column takes much more space than most names need, leaving only 115px for conditions.

critique.good: The wider conditions column gives prose a more natural rhythm and makes the table substantially easier to read. Delivery ranges and headers stay intact, and rows remain clearly distinguished.
critique.problems: Metro Manila and Greater Luzon each wrap onto two lines, while Remote island areas takes three. This makes the destination column less immediately scannable.
critique.cause: At 103px, the destination column has only 82px of text width; most of the remaining space is assigned to the 171px conditions column.

critique.good: Most destination names fit on one line, Remote island areas wraps neatly, and the delivery windows remain intact.
critique.problems: Conditions are noticeably more fragmented than in r0B, producing taller rows and more empty space in the first two columns. The gain in destination scanning comes at a considerable cost to prose readability.
critique.cause: The 130px destination column leaves 144px for conditions, 27px less than in r0B.

critique.good: The header hierarchy is clear, delivery ranges stay on one line, and the destination names remain readily identifiable. Remote island areas occupies two lines, giving the row labels a reasonably compact rhythm.
critique.problems: Conditions remain narrow and make the rows tall, leaving large empty areas beneath the short labels and windows. Metro Manila and Greater Luzon each wrap, though both remain easy to read.
critique.cause: The 166px Conditions column carries almost all the prose; the 108px Destination column provides enough room for island areas together but not the two longer destination names.

critique.good: Metro Manila fits on one line, and the destination column is comfortable to scan. The ranges and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The conditions break into many short lines, especially for Greater Luzon and Remote island areas. The resulting tall rows and large empty cells weaken the connection between each destination, its window, and its conditions.
critique.cause: Increasing Destination to 118px leaves only 156px for Conditions. The extra space benefits one row label but makes the lengthy prose substantially taller.

critique.good: The wider Conditions column gives the prose a better rhythm and makes the table shorter than the other two designs. Windows and headers stay intact, and each row remains clearly separated.
critique.problems: Remote island areas breaks over three lines, making that label less compact than in r1A. The prose still creates tall rows with considerable blank space in the first two columns.
critique.cause: Destination is 103px wide, leaving 82px for text, so island areas cannot fit together. Conditions receives 171px, but the long qualifications still require many lines.

critique.good: Headers are clear, delivery ranges stay on one line, and the destination labels remain easy to scan. Remote island areas wraps into two balanced lines.
critique.problems: Conditions form narrow, tall blocks, making comparisons across rows laborious and leaving substantial empty space beside the prose.
critique.cause: The 167px Conditions column has only 146px for text. The 107px Destination column preserves a useful two-line label but leaves less room for conditions.

critique.good: The 171px Conditions column improves the Greater Luzon paragraph by one line, while all delivery ranges and headers remain intact. Destinations are still identifiable at a glance.
critique.problems: Remote island areas breaks into three short lines, weakening the rhythm of the row labels. Conditions remain tall and narrow, with considerable empty space in the other columns.
critique.cause: Reducing Destination to 103px leaves too little text width for “island areas” on one line. The additional 4px given to Conditions helps only some of its line breaks.

critique.good: Destination labels have the same readable wrapping as r2A, and the headers remain clear.
critique.problems: The Greater Luzon and Mindanao delivery ranges separate from “days,” making the commitments harder to scan. Conditions remain as tall as in r2A.
critique.cause: The 84px Window column leaves just too little room for the wider ranges and their unit; the 167px Conditions column is unchanged from r2A.

understanding.purpose: Help readers find the delivery window and any qualifying conditions for a destination.
understanding.reading: Readers scan destination names down the first column, then read across the row to compare delivery windows and check the conditions. Longer conditions will set much of the row height, leaving room for some destination names to wrap.
groups: Window and Conditions belong under Delivery: the window gives the commitment, while the conditions qualify it.
keep_intact: Delivery ranges and their unit, such as 2–3 days
Unbreakable words in destination names and conditions
Times and other identifiers within conditions
may_wrap: Multiword destination names at word boundaries
Conditions as prose at natural word boundaries

bad.why: Two delivery windows break between the numeric range and “days,” making the values less consistent and harder to compare down the column.

final.rationale: The preferred designs give the long conditions text most of the width while keeping every delivery window on one line. Their bold destination labels remain recognizable even when wrapped, and the spanning Delivery header keeps the two related columns together. The wider destination column in r1B keeps Metro Manila on one line and Remote island areas on two, but leaves noticeably narrower conditions and taller rows.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading task; columns with different roles need not be equally wide.
Keep compact values and their units together when readers need to compare them down a column.
Judge wrapping across complete rows, including the whitespace created beside long cells.
specific: Conditions contains much more text than the destination and window columns, so it benefits most from the available width.
At 84px, the Window column wraps some values; the rendered candidates at 85px and 86px keep them intact.

final.tradeoffs: A wider destination column makes row labels quicker to scan, especially Remote island areas, but takes space from the conditions. The preferred designs accept a three-line label to give the recurring prose more room.
final.uncertain: A designer who prioritizes finding destinations over reading conditions could reasonably prefer r2A or r1B. The ranges are conservative estimates from the rendered candidates; intermediate widths and independent endpoint combinations have not been verified.

A.why: Conditions have useful space, but two delivery windows break across lines while the others stay together, making comparison uneven.

B.why: Every delivery window stays on one line, destination labels remain recognizable, and conditions have a reasonable share of the width.

C.why: All delivery windows stay intact and the slightly wider conditions column improves the prose; Remote island areas wraps to three lines.

D.why: Delivery windows stay intact and Metro Manila fits on one line, but the narrower conditions column creates more short lines and taller rows.

E.why: The near-equal columns give excessive space to short delivery windows and leave conditions in a very narrow, heavily wrapped column.

F.why: Conditions have the most room, but every delivery window splits the number from days, weakening the column's usefulness for quick comparison.

reviews.unsure: B preserves Remote island areas in two lines, while C gives the conditions slightly more room; their trade-off is close.

A.why: All delivery windows stay on one line, and the conditions have useful room. Destination names wrap naturally, though the conditions remain dense.

B.why: The conditions gain a little room, but every delivery window splits its number from 'days', making comparisons slower; the last destination also takes three lines.

C.why: The conditions have reasonable space, but some delivery windows wrap and others do not, creating an uneven comparison column.

D.why: Delivery windows stay intact and Metro Manila fits on one line, but the extra destination width leaves the long conditions noticeably narrower.

E.why: The nearly equal columns leave excessive space around short delivery windows and squeeze conditions into very short lines, producing tall, fragmented rows.

F.why: All delivery windows stay on one line, and the conditions receive the most room among layouts that keep them intact. The last destination wraps to three lines.

reviews.unsure: A keeps the last destination to two lines, while F gives the conditions slightly more space; the small trade-off is difficult to rank decisively from the renders.
